narrative.overview: Kavya Chocolat should feel like standing at a small chocolate studio's counter: a sheet of warm cream paper, a burgundy lacquer panel, a brass ruler, and four bars laid out like specimens with their tasting notes. The system is editorial rather than promotional. It uses ruled structure, generous margins, and one confident display face to make a modest catalogue feel considered. It refuses the centred-hero-plus-three-icon-cards storefront, glossy gradients, floating rounded cards, and decoration that does not carry information. Burgundy is a field, not a highlight: the announcement rule, the footer, the admin rail, the hero plate, and selected panels. Cream paper carries most of the page. Brass is a drafting line â€” borders, rules, small numerals â€” and has a separate, darker text variant so it never fails contrast on paper. Photography is large, warm, and quiet; the interface stays out of its way. Motion is restrained: a single rise-and-fade on first paint, 160â€“180ms state transitions, and nothing that loops. The fixed paper grain is the only ambient texture.
keyCharacteristics: Warm cream paper (#f6efe3) with a 3.5% fixed grain overlay.
Burgundy (#75212f) as structural field, not accent sprinkles.
Sharp 2px corners; 1px brass-toned hairlines; no rounded cards.
One family (Sen) for display, UI, body, and money; hierarchy from weight, size, and case.
Sen 600 headlines at tight tracking; 400 body; 600 uppercase labels. No second face, no italic.
Flat by default; depth from tonal fields and hairlines, not drop shadows.

rules.name: The Burgundy Field Rule
rules.body: Burgundy is applied as a complete field â€” a bar, a rail, a plate, a footer â€” not as confetti. A screen may have several burgundy fields; it should not have burgundy dots, pills, and underlines scattered between them.

rules.name: The Brass Contrast Rule
rules.body: Brass #b08a57 is a line color on light grounds, never a text color. Text that should read as brass uses Brass Ink on paper and Brass Light on burgundy.

rules.name: The Paper Majority Rule
rules.body: Cream paper remains the dominant surface. If burgundy covers more than roughly a third of a storefront screen, the screen is probably a campaign surface, not a catalogue page.

rules.name: The 11px Floor Rule
rules.body: Functional text â€” links, labels, buttons, table cells, metadata that carries meaning â€” never goes below 11px, including inside the footer. Only non-interactive legal smallprint may sit at 10px, and even that is discouraged.

rules.name: The One-Family Rule
rules.body: Sen carries every word on the page. Display headings are Sen 600 with tight tracking, labels are Sen 600 uppercase and tracked, body is Sen 400. A second typeface, a script face, or a fabricated italic is off-system.

rules.name: The Mixed-Case Body Rule
rules.body: Body copy is sentence case. Uppercase is reserved for short labels, eyebrows, and buttons, with tracking added to compensate.

rules.name: The Ruled Not Boxed Rule
rules.body: Prefer a 1px rule and spacing over a bordered, shadowed card. Panels are for forms, admin data, and the cart drawer; editorial content sits directly on paper.

rules.name: The Flat-By-Default Rule
rules.body: If a surface can be separated with a rule or a tonal shift, do not give it a shadow. Shadows signal something floating above the page, not a section boundary.

rules.name: The Two-Corner Rule
rules.body: Everything structural is 2px; only tags and status pills go round. A rounded content card is off-system.

dos: Do keep cream paper as the majority surface and use burgundy as a complete field.
Do use 11px as the functional-text floor and 12px+ for body metadata where space allows.
Do use Brass Ink for text on paper and Brass Light for text on burgundy.
Do separate sections with 1px hairlines and spacing before reaching for a card or shadow.
Do label placeholders visibly: "Placeholder price Â· tax not configured", "placeholder photograph" in alt text, "Tax (not configured)".
Do keep one primary button per decision area and make the next action obvious.
Do preserve the logo's proportions and clear space; use the knockout version on burgundy.
Do keep numbers tabular (.num) in prices, totals, stock, and tables.
donts: Don't use brass #b08a57 as text on paper or cream; it fails 4.5:1.
Don't set functional text below 11px, including footer links and metadata.
Don't round content cards, images, or panels beyond 2px, or introduce a second corner language.
Don't scatter burgundy across small dots, pills, and underlines instead of committing to a field.
Don't use gradients except as photographic scrims over images.
Don't introduce a second typeface, a script face, or a synthetic italic; Sen's variable weights carry display, notes, and UI.
Don't invent reviews, ratings, certifications, nutrition panels, or health claims to fill a layout.
Don't describe jaggery as sugar-free, or an order as paid, or an email as sent while email is unconfigured.
Don't hide admin actions behind navigation alone; every protected action is server-verified, and the UI should reflect that seriousness.
